steps.message:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station T-11, survey area T. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 82.6 | 5.04 | 5.04
2 | 162.4 | 1.62 | 6.66
3 | 121.3 | 2.57 | 9.23
4 | 152.0 | 0.91 | 10.14
5 | 105.9 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as QHK-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station T-11, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

**Site Note – Station T-11, Survey Area T**

The VES interpretation yields a 5-layer resistivity model with depths to base at 5.04, 6.66, 9.23, and 10.14 m, and resistivities of 82.6, 162.4, 121.3, 152.0, and 105.9 Ω·m respectively (layer 5 unbounded).

Applying the standard curve-type convention to consecutive triplets:
- Layers 1-2-3: 82.6 < 162.4 > 121.3 → K
- Layers 2-3-4: 162.4 > 121.3 < 152.0 → H
- Layers 3-4-5: 121.3 < 152.0 > 105.9 → K

This gives a curve type of **KHK**, not QHK as stated in the file. The first triplet shows a rise then fall in resistivity (K), not a steady decrease (Q) as the "Q" label would imply. The drilling team should treat the subsurface as a K-H-K sequence (resistive layer over conductive layer over resistive basal layer, with intermediate undulations) rather than the filed classification.

Recommend updating the interpretation record to correct the curve-type label before finalizing lithological correlations.
